brokers.name: Interactive Brokers (IBKR)
brokers.who_can_open: Both. Canada and the US are both on IBKR's list of countries where accounts can be opened; Canadian clients are served by Interactive Brokers Canada Inc., US clients by Interactive Brokers LLC.

regulator.canada: Interactive Brokers Canada Inc.: member of CIRO; Member - CIPF. Order-execution-only dealer.
regulator.us: Interactive Brokers LLC: member NYSE - FINRA - SIPC; regulated by the SEC (and CFTC).

brokers.commission_us_stocks: IBKR Fixed: USD 0.005 per share, USD 1.00 minimum, maximum 1% of trade value (plus regulatory fees). IBKR Lite: US exchange-listed stocks and ETFs commission-free for US retail investors (with exceptions); Lite availability to Canadian residents unverified.
brokers.commission_cdn_stocks: IBKR Canada Fixed: CAD 0.01 per share, CAD 1.00 minimum, maximum 0.5% of trade value (CAD-denominated). USD-denominated Canadian listings: USD 0.008/share, USD 0.80 min, 0.4% max.
brokers.registered_accounts: Canada: TFSA, RRSP, FHSA, RRIF (RRIF launched Feb 3, 2026). US: Traditional, Traditional Rollover, Traditional Inherited, Roth, Roth Inherited, SEP and SIMPLE IRAs.

names: TWS API (runs through Trader Workstation / IB Gateway)
IBKR Web API (Client Portal Gateway for retail clients)
public_api.requirements: IBKR: 'Clients with fully open and funded accounts may use our Web API's Trading features to trade their accounts immediately.' Using a paper account with the Web API requires the linked live account to be fully open, funded and an IBKR Pro account. Unfunded trial accounts do not support the API. FIX for individuals: unverified.
public_api.ai_connection: IBKR AI Integration connects ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Perplexity and other MCP tools to the account via an IBKR-hosted MCP server; the client reviews and submits every order. Separately, IBKR Autonomous Trading (announced Oct 21, 2026) lets connected AI submit supported orders without per-order approval inside a dedicated 'AI Partition'; limited to individual, non-margin accounts (no joint, retirement, advisor, organizational or Lite accounts) and requires 10 trades of $100+ over two weeks in Review & Approve mode first; availability varies by IBKR entity and country (Canada not stated). AI Integration is not available in India or Japan.

brokers.paper_trading: Yes. 'All IBKR clients have the ability to open a paper trading account'; a paper account comes with every account, and can be used (with delayed data) before funding.
brokers.known_for: Per-share pricing and access to many global markets from one account.
recent_changes: AI Integration via MCP; IBKR Autonomous Trading announced Oct 21, 2026
unverified: IBKR Lite availability for Canadian residents
Whether AI Integration works with paper accounts

rules.topic: US: pattern day trader rule replaced by intraday margin
rules.summary: FINRA amended Rule 4210 to replace the day-trading margin rules, including the trade-count 'pattern day trader' designation and the $25,000 minimum equity, with intraday margin standards. SEC approved April 14, 2026 (Release 34-105226). Regulatory Notice 26-10 (Apr 20, 2026): effective June 4, 2026, but brokers may phase in until Oct 20, 2027, so a reader's broker may still apply the old PDT rule and $25,000 minimum. Under the new rule: no PDT label by trade count; 25% maintenance margin on long margin-eligible equities throughout the day (firms may require more); under $2,000 equity you can trade in a margin account but without leverage. FINRA tells investors to ask their own firm when it switches.

In a cash account you must pay in full by settlement (generally one day after the trade for most securities); firms apply Regulation T and can restrict trading after a violation. Good-faith and freeriding specifics were not on the page read (unverified).

rules.topic: US: auto-trading services and AI claims
rules.summary: FINRA (July 29, 2025) warns about auto-trading services from unregistered entities: their trades may not fit your goals, losses can build before you notice, AI claims may be exaggerated, never hand over your brokerage username and password, check firms on BrokerCheck, and keep monitoring your account even with regulated services. The SEC has charged advisers for false claims about using AI ('AI washing', Mar 18, 2024).

At order-execution-only (OEO) dealers, which include all the Canadian self-directed brokers listed, clients make their own investment decisions; the dealer gives no recommendations and no suitability assessment (CIRO's 'Recommendation Prohibition'). CIRO consulted (comments due Feb 26, 2025) on letting OEO dealers offer non-tailored tools and information. CIRO research (May 26, 2026) describes OEO investors as people comfortable making their own decisions and found concrete risk examples at decision points cut high-risk activity, while tick-box acknowledgements did not. CIRO's main OEO guidance page could not be read (robots).

rules.topic: Canada: AI and securities law; AI-branded scams
rules.summary: CSA Staff Notice and Consultation 11-348 (Dec 5, 2024) explains how existing securities law applies to AI systems in capital markets and does not create new legal requirements. CSA keeps investor alerts on AI-branded trading platforms (e.g., 'Quantum AI', 'Capital Market AI'). Whether Canada has a PDT-style rule: none found (unverified).

rules.topic: You remain responsible for every order
rules.summary: Brokers that let AI connect say the account holder owns the orders: IBKR says you are responsible for reviewing AI-generated instructions and deciding whether to turn them into orders; Questrade requires you to approve every order in its app; Public says trades submitted through its MCP server are 'deemed authorized by you'; Robinhood and IBKR Autonomous Trading allow orders without per-order approval if you set it up that way.

rules.topic: API trading for your own account is usually allowed
rules.summary: Several brokers explicitly offer personal-use APIs that place orders in the holder's own account: IBKR (open and funded accounts can trade via Web API immediately), E*TRADE (individual key tied to one user), Tradier (personal API token), Public (personal, non-commercial use), Schwab (Trader API - Individual), Webull (individual Trading API after review), Alpaca (API-first). Exceptions: Questrade's API trading is for partner developers only (its MCP drafts orders you approve); no public API found at Wealthsimple, Fidelity or the Canadian bank-owned brokers. Distributing an app to other people generally needs partner/vendor approval (E*TRADE vendor keys, Tradier Partner status, Public bars offering apps to third parties).

anthropic.topic: Usage Policy in force now (effective Sept 15, 2025)
anthropic.summary: Anthropic's Usage Policy treats financial uses (with legal and employment uses) as high-risk use cases that need extra safeguards: a "human in the loop" to oversee outputs and disclosure that AI is involved. Anthropic's Aug 15, 2025 post says these requirements apply to outputs that reach consumers, not to business-to-business use.

anthropic.topic: 2026 Usage Policy update (published Oct 8, 2026; effective Nov 12, 2026)
anthropic.summary: Finance is one of 11 high-risk areas. It covers personalized recommendations to buy, sell, hold or allocate among specific investment products (securities, funds, digital assets, annuities) and personal tax advice. For such a recommendation, a qualified person (with the relevant training or experience and any required licence) must review the output before it reaches the individual or is used to carry out a decision, must have authority to change it, and stays responsible for it; the individual must be told AI was used (naming Claude is not required). Not covered: general financial education not applied to someone's own situation, internal research and drafting. The requirements apply to anyone using Anthropic's products, not only businesses. The text does not say how they apply when the user and the person getting the advice are the same, and it does not specifically address an agent executing trades; users are responsible for actions their agents take through connected systems. Anthropic says the core high-risk requirements are unchanged in substance from the earlier policy.
anthropic.relevance_to_be_the_puck: A guide on using Claude with Be The Puck's data to draft orders the reader reviews and approves themselves sits closer to the education and drafting side, and keeps the reader as the decision-maker. If Be The Puck itself used Claude to send personalized buy/sell output to readers, the high-risk requirements (qualified human review and AI disclosure) would apply. This is a reading of the policy, not legal advice.
